newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to attend Arafat conference if invited.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to attend Arafat conference if invited.

text.p: The United States will attend an international meeting called by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to discuss the Middle East peace deadlock if it is formally invited, the State Department said on Tuesday.

"We're aware that Chairman Arafat has called for a conference on Saturday in Gaza. We certainly, if an invitation is formally issued to the United States, will be there," department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.

The PLO leader wants U.S., European and Arab envoys to discuss a crisis brewing since Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu approved plans to build Jewish housing between Arab East Jerusalem and Bethlehem.

But Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy, in a hastily convened news conference, said such a meeting would violate agreements and warned that PLO efforts to bring international pressure on Israel could freeze peace moves.
Burns said the United States would be represented at such a meeting by its consul-general in Jerusalem, Edward Abington.

"We do understand the frustration of the Palestinian leadership. They've been buffeted by some fairly significant Israeli government decisions over the last couple of weeks. Chairman Arafat obviously feels the need to talk to friendly countries around the world, and that's appropriate," Burns told a news briefing.
